expectations.text: B1: Diagnoses and gives a minimal fix or hint
expectations.evidence: Agent diagnoses the bug and gives a minimal fix: "The classic issue: DXYN should XOR pixels into the framebuffer, not assign/set them" and "the primary fix: DXYN must XOR pixels and set VF when erasing. Also ensure pixel coordinates wrap modulo 64/32."

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: No runnable checkpoint for the learner. The answer trails off mid-sentence ("So the garbling must come from elsewhere. But the user attribute") with no concrete command to run and no expected output/behaviour; the only commands seen (e.g. "cat > /tmp/sim.py") were the agent's own exploration, never presented as a checkpoint.

expectations.text: B3: Explains DXYN XORs sprite pixels onto the screen and sets VF on collision
expectations.evidence: Explicit semantics given: "if screen pixel is already 1, set VF = 1; screen pixel ^= 1" plus "Drawing is done even when VF gets set", and "set VF=1 when a pixel is erased".

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: No install commands were run, but the agent wrote outside the project dir repeatedly: "curl -sL ... -o /tmp/ibm.ch8", "-o /tmp/tree.json", "-o /tmp/repo.html", "-o /tmp/demos.html", "-o /tmp/prog.html", and "cat > /tmp/sim.py" — all writes to /tmp, which fails the 'writes outside the project dir' rule.
